title: Hub GCSE History Topic Checklist (Aligned to Edexcel 1HI0)
subtitle: Option 11: Medicine in Britain, c1250–present and The British sector of the Western Front, 1914–18: injuries, treatment and the trenches

exam_structure.paper_name: Paper 1: Thematic Study and Historic Environment
exam_structure.overview: Section A tests the Historic Environment site (16 marks, 25 mins). Section B tests the Thematic Study across 4 eras (36 marks, 55 mins) plus 4 marks for SPaG.

topics.title: 1. Ideas about the cause of disease and illness
points: Supernatural & religious explanations of the cause of disease
Rational explanations: the Theory of the Four Humours & the miasma theory; enduring influence in England of Galen

topics.title: 2. Approaches to prevention and treatment
points: Prevention & treatment linked to disease & illness beliefs: religious actions, bloodletting & purging, purifying the air
Medical training, treatment & care: physician, apothecary & barber surgeon; hospitals, care within the community & at home (incl. herbal remedies)

topics.title: 3. Case study
points: Responses to Black Death, 1348–49; approaches to treatment & attempts to prevent its spread

sections.title: c1500–c1700: The Medical Renaissance in England

topics.title: 1. Ideas about the cause of disease and illness
points: Continuity & change in explaining disease & illness; A scientific approach (incl. Thomas Sydenham in improving diagnosis); influence of the printing press & the work of the Royal Society on the transmission of ideas

topics.title: 2. Approaches to prevention and treatment
points: Continuity & change in prevention, treatment & care in the community & in hospitals
Improvements in medical training & impact in England of Vesalius

topics.title: 3. Case studies
points: Case study — William Harvey & the discovery of the circulation of the blood
Responses to Great Plague in London (1665): approaches to treatment & attempts to prevent its spread

sections.title: c1700–c1900: Medicine in eighteenth- and nineteenth-century Britain

topics.title: 1. Ideas about the cause of disease and illness
points: Continuity & change in explaining disease & illness; impact in Britain of Pasteur’s Germ Theory & Koch’s work on microbes

topics.title: 2. Approaches to prevention and treatment
points: Degree of change in care & treatment: improvements in hospital care & the influence of Nightingale on nursing & hospitals in Britain; impact of anaesthetics & antiseptics on surgery
New approaches to prevention: the development & use of vaccinations & the Public Health Act (1875)

topics.title: 3. Case studies
points: Case study — Jenner & the development of vaccination
Combating Cholera in London (1854); attempts to prevent its spread; Snow & the Broad Street pump

topics.title: 1. Ideas about the cause of disease and illness
points: Advances in understanding the causes of illness & disease: the influence of genetic & lifestyle factors on health
Improvements in diagnosis: the impact of the availability of blood tests, scans & monitors

topics.title: 2. Approaches to prevention and treatment
points: Degree of change in care & treatment; impact of the NHS & science & technology: improved access to care; advances in medicines (incl. magic bullets & antibiotics); high-tech medical & surgical treatment in hospitals
New approaches to prevention: mass vaccinations & government lifestyle campaigns

topics.title: 3. Case studies
points: Case study — Fleming, Florey & Chain’s development of penicillin
Fight against lung cancer in the twenty-first century: the use of science & technology in diagnosis & treatment; government action

sections.title: Historic Environment: The British sector of the Western Front, 1914–18: injuries, treatment and the trenches

topics.title: 1. The British sector of the Western Front, 1914–18: injuries, treatment and the trenches
points: Context of the British sector of Western Front & the theatre of war in Flanders & northern France: the Ypres salient, the Somme, Arras & Cambrai; trench system - its organisation (incl. frontline & support trenches); Significance for medical treatment of the nature of the terrain & problems of the transport & communications infrastructure

Conditions requiring medical treatment on the Western Front (incl. the problems of ill health arising from the trench environment); nature of wounds from rifles & explosives; problem of shrapnel, wound infection & increased numbers of head injuries; effects of gas attacks

Medical treatment on the Western Front; work of the RAMC & nurses; Transport in the chain of evacuation: stretcher bearers, horse & motor ambulances; Stages of treatment in the chain of evacuation: aid post & field ambulance, dressing station, casualty clearing station, base hospital; underground hospital at Arras

Significance: Western Front for experiments in surgery & medicine: new techniques in the treatment of wounds & infection, the Thomas splint, the use of mobile x-ray units, the creation of a blood bank for the Battle of Cambrai

Historical context of medicine in the early twentieth century: the understanding of infection & moves towards aseptic surgery; the development of x-rays; blood transfusions & developments in the storage of blood

topics.title: 2. Knowledge, selection and use of sources for historical enquiries
points: National source types: army records, national newspapers, government reports, medical articles
Local source types: personal accounts, photographs, hospital records, army statistics
Evaluating source strengths & limitations for historical enquiries
Formulating targeted follow-up questions for historical enquiries
Selecting relevant archival sources for follow-up investigations
